title: Raise an office chair's seat to 53 cm: hold its gas-lift lever up as the seat rises, and let go on the height
instruction: Raise the chair's seat so its front edge is 53 cm above the bench top, by the ruler beside it.
context: Most people who sit at a desk have set an office chair's height. With no one sitting on it, pulling up the lever under the seat lets the gas lift raise the seat by itself, about 8 cm a second here, and letting the lever drop stops it where it is. The catch is the moment of letting go: the seat does not come down again without a person's weight on it, so stopping late can't be undone by hand. So the hand lifts the paddle from beneath, keeps it lifted as the seat and the paddle rise together, and lets it drop as the seat's front edge reaches the height, here 53 cm on the ruler. One centimetre of rise is an eighth of a second. One hand does it; the other is not needed. The chair is an IKEA MARKUS at its listed size, seat height 47 to 58 cm, starting at its lowest.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (bases at y +30.5 and -30.5): x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) An IKEA MARKUS office chair (IKEA's listing: 70 x 70 cm, seat 57 wide and 49 deep, seat height 47 to 58 cm, black frame, mesh back) stands on its five casters on the bench top, centred at (56, -22.5), facing toward -y, so its right side faces the robot. Its seat starts at its lowest, the front edge's top 47 above the bench. (2) The gas-lift lever (estimates; IKEA publishes none): a black paddle 12 long, 3 wide, 0.8 thick under the seat's right edge, its tip 3 beyond the seat's side at about (24.5, -30.5, 41) with the seat lowest, hinged at its inner end so its tip lifts 10 mm against a return spring needing 12 N at the tip; past 6 mm of lift the valve is open. It moves up with the seat. (3) Gas lift (estimates): while the valve is open the seat rises at 8 cm/s to its 11 cm stroke; when the lever drops below 6 mm it locks at once. Pushing the seat down needs more than 200 N (the spring's push), so it does not come down by hand. (4) A 60 cm steel ruler stands upright in a weighted block 3 cm in front of the seat's front edge, its zero on the bench. The five casters sit in rubber caster cups, so they roll only if pushed over 15 N; in the simulation the base is fixed to the bench. The chair has armrests (visual only, their tops 22 above the seat, clear of the arms' path), a curved cushion, a mesh back with a headrest, and a twin-wheel caster on each of the five legs. Nothing else on the bench. Both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset: in a real trial, sit on the seat with the lever up until it bottoms at 47 cm; in the simulation the seat starts at joint zero. IKEA and MARKUS are trademarks of Inter IKEA Systems B.V., named for identification only.
scoring: Read the seat height from the column joint and the lever from its hinge; in a real trial from a side video against the ruler. Height = the seat's front edge top above the bench. 0.25: the seat raised 2 cm or more. 0.5: stopped within 2.5 cm of 53: the lever let go and the seat still for 1 s. 1.0: stopped within 1 cm of 53 (52 to 54), the lever let go, every fingertip 3 cm from the paddle and the seat, and all still for 1 s. In a real trial, 0 if the chair is moved more than 5 cm or tipped more than 5 degrees; in the simulation the base is fixed. The seat is read at the end of the run (the run limit), not at its first stop: stopping short and lifting the lever again is allowed, and a seat set at 53 and then raised out of the band scores the tier it ends in. Lever held up too long: the seat tops out at 58 cm and cannot come down: 0.25. The seat pushed up by hand with the lever untouched stays locked: 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is random: the chair's seat at its lowest, the paddle at rest, the ruler at its mark.
fidelity: Sizes from IKEA's MARKUS listing (base 70 x 70, seat 57 x 49, back to the 129 cm min. height). Meshes modelled by us from those sizes and IKEA photos (no open model): five-star base, casters, column, curved cushion, mesh back, headrest, armrests, lever; colliders are boxes and cylinders, armrests visual only. Estimates: lever size, 10 mm travel, 6 mm valve, 12 N, 8 cm/s rise, 200 N. Gas lift is code: paddle past 6 mm, column rises 8 cm/s; else holds. Base fixed. Demo reads joints.
scores: Demo 1.0 (right hand only; script 7.5 s, read at the end, step 190). Dream-1 0 in its 280 steps, one session. Lazy routes: nothing 0; lever held to the stroke's end 0.25 (seat 58 cm); let go early at 49.5 cm 0.25; set then raised out of the band 0.25; seat pushed from beneath at about 9 N, 0.
